decisions.decision: Push mode only for now — fling mode UI hidden, selectedMode hardcoded to 'push'
decisions.rationale: Ship a polished single mode rather than two half-finished modes

decisions.decision: Vanilla JS + Matter.js, no build system, Canvas 2D
decisions.rationale: No build complexity for a game of this scope; Matter.js loaded via CDN
Modern, fast, ESM-native — compatible with the project's ES6 module structure

decisions.decision: Add hit combo multiplier to push mode: each hit within 1s raises damage by 0.5×, capped at 3.0×
decisions.rationale: Rewards skilled rapid swinging without changing the core one-hit-ideal scoring loop

decisions.decision: Keep fling mode as a selectable second mode; push mode is the default and primary
decisions.rationale: Both mechanics are worth keeping — push for sustained swinging, fling for projectile precision

decisions.rationale: Simplify the codebase to a single polished mode; fling was never the primary experience and adds dead code

decisions.decision: Items 35+36 combined: PointerEvents API in input.js + CSS transform scaling via fitToViewport() in main.js
decisions.rationale: Single codepath for mouse and touch; getBoundingClientRect in getCanvasXY automatically compensates for CSS scale transform, so no coordinate math changes needed anywhere

decisions.decision: Damage formula: speed² × angleFactor × material.yoyoDamage × impactMultiplier × comboMultiplier / DAMAGE_SCALE (1200), replacing linear speed/15
decisions.rationale: Speed-squared creates a meaningful skill ceiling: 1-hit possible at max speed (~450 px/step), 3 hits at good play (~250 px/step), casual players take 5-9 hits. Glass/wood shield breakSpeeds lowered from 140/300 to 100/180 — wood shield at 300 was unreachable. DAMAGE_SCALE is a single named constant for easy post-play tuning.

decisions.decision: Tail-attachment redesign (combined #46+#47): move the rat's swing constraint from its center to a tail-base anchor point, paired with mass/frictionAir tuning on both variants; the rope visual (drawString) is replaced by the rat's own tail stretching to the pivot, and rotation switches from accumulated spinAngle to physics-driven body.angle
decisions.rationale: An off-center attachment lets gravity naturally torque the rat to hang below the grip point — literally 'held by the tail' — while also being the most direct, lowest-risk lever for the weightless feel (#47), since it doesn't touch collision detection, fragment spawning, or the damage formula. A two-body ragdoll rat was considered and rejected as architecturally oversized for this scope.

decisions.decision: Tail-attachment rebalance settled after 4 rounds of playtesting. Final values — standard rat: mass 1.0→4.5, frictionAir 0.005→0.025, restitution 0.35→0.05; heavy rat: mass 3.5→11.5, frictionAir 0.003→0.015, restitution 0.1→0.02; constraint stiffness 0.65→0.35
decisions.rationale: The first two tuning passes (mass/frictionAir increases, stiffness decreases) weren't enough — user reported no major difference. The decisive change was reversing frictionAir direction to a sharp ~5x increase (faster momentum decay, more effort to reach top speed) and dropping rat restitution near zero (less bounce, more hit-and-slide). Accepted as good for now. Caveat: Matter.js resolves collision restitution as max(rat, target), so steel targets (restitution 0.55 in target.js) will still bounce regardless of the rat's value — a target.js follow-up if that surfaces during task 45's full playthrough.

decisions.decision: Heavier impact feedback (supersedes #48, expanded to include rat body-wear): extend particles.js with a rotating 'chunk' shape; on every HP-damage hit, fire three damage-scaled bursts (red blood splash, target-material chunk debris via material.crackedColor, rat-fur chunk debris via a new variant color); reuse the already-generated-but-unrendered yoyo.plugin.crackPattern to draw scuff marks on the rat's body via drawCracks(), plus an HP-based body color blend toward a new worn tone
decisions.rationale: Builds entirely on existing systems — particles.js's emit/update/draw loop, target.js's crackedColor palette, and main.js's dormant per-hit crackPattern generation for the rat body — so no new physics bodies or rendering pipelines are needed. This keeps the change low-risk and avoids the perf cost of spawning Matter.js fragments on every combo hit (a physics-debris approach was considered and rejected for that reason). The new 'chunk' particle shape gives debris a distinct angular silhouette from the round blood splashes.

decisions.decision: Heavier impact feedback rebalanced after playtesting: chunk/debris particle radius now scales from 1x (current size, at damageIntensity 0) up to 3x (at damageIntensity 1) instead of a fixed size; chunk-shaped particles also have an 8% chance to spawn 2.5x-4x oversized for rare visual variety; SHATTER-time giblet fragments render as one of 4 random shapes (blob/triangle/rect/diamond) instead of always ellipses
decisions.rationale: First playtesting pass found the fixed debris size didn't read as more impactful on harder hits, and the uniform ellipse giblets looked repetitive on shatter. Scaling radius with damageIntensity (already used for particle count) ties debris size directly to hit strength with no new state; the 8% oversized roll and shapeType variety (physics.js fragment plugin field, consumed in renderer.js drawFragments) add visual variance cheaply since both reuse existing per-particle/per-fragment data.

decisions.decision: Four-part tuning/feature round (tasks 63-74), surfaced during task 45's playthrough: (1) recalibrate speed meter + damage formula — pushMaxSpeed ×1.25 (standard 600→750, heavy 500→625) and DAMAGE_SCALE 1200→2000, with the shake-threshold and damageIntensity-saturation constants rescaled ×0.6 to match — so the realistic top swing speed reads as 60% on the meter and 1-hit shatters require near-max effort/combo; (2) shape variety — convert 3 rectangle targets (levels 1, 3, 7) to circles; (3) a new moving-target mechanic — static bodies repositioned via Body.setPosition along a sine wave, driven by a `movement: { axis, range, period }` level schema field, applied to levels 6 and 9; (4) replace the 4 geometric giblet fragment shapes with organic jittered-radius 'flesh chunk' blobs; (5) shorten/soften the rat's swing trail by activating the previously-dormant per-variant trailLength field (20/12 vs the global cap of 30) and lowering the trail's alpha multiplier
decisions.rationale: Recalibration keeps the meter/damage relationship internally consistent (pushMaxSpeed and DAMAGE_SCALE scaled by inverse factors) while raising the skill ceiling, rather than just rescaling the HUD. Moving targets reuse static bodies + Body.setPosition so collision/damage formulas need no changes — a dynamic-body approach was rejected as unnecessary complexity. Giblet blobs and trail tone-down both activate/reuse existing per-fragment and per-variant data rather than adding new state, consistent with this project's preference for repurposing dormant fields.

decisions.decision: Corrected the task-63 damage recalibration: DAMAGE_SCALE 2000→200 (a 10x cut), with damageIntensity's saturation point (24→240) and the screen-shake damage threshold (12→120, shakeIntensity divisor 8→80) scaled by the same factor to preserve their relative tuning; CLAUDE.md's HP system and Impact feedback bullets updated, and the now-disproven '~450px/60%=realistic ceiling' claim removed pending real swing-speed data.
decisions.rationale: Playtesting the tasks 63-74 round found Level 1 took 30-40 hits to clear versus the ~2-3 hits the task-63 calibration targeted — the underlying assumption (real swings reach ~60% of the new 750 pushMaxSpeed, i.e. ~450 px/step) was wrong; actual swings land far slower. DAMAGE_SCALE is the direct lever (damage is linear in 1/DAMAGE_SCALE, so hit-count scales ~linearly with it), and a straight 10x cut maps 30-40 hits to the requested ~3-4. damageIntensity and the shake threshold were tuned as a set with DAMAGE_SCALE=2000 last round, so scaling them by the same 10x keeps particle-burst and shake feel consistent with that pass's intent rather than maxing out on every routine hit. pushMaxSpeed/meter calibration is left untouched — it doesn't feed the damage formula, so it's an independent follow-up once real speed data exists.

decisions.decision: Game-feel bundle design (supersedes tasks 81/82/83/87/89 with tasks 93-98): inline integration (approach A) — hit-stop as a main.js timer gating the sim block (physics + gameplay timers pause, particles/shake/render continue) on the shared damage > 120 threshold, 40-80ms scaled by damageIntensity; ~2-frame white flash + velocity-aligned squash-stretch in drawRat; ground-only blood decal offscreen canvas cleared on restart; audio master GainNode -> DynamicsCompressor bus with a persisted mute toggle (no volume slider); looping whoosh tracking the 0-1 normalizedSpeed. Implementation gated behind tasks 76/45 playtests validating the current branch.
decisions.rationale: Approach A (inline, no new module) chosen for smallest blast radius over a dedicated juice.js module (abstraction ahead of need — one collision event, one consumer) and an event bus (oversized). Physics-only freeze chosen because a full render freeze reads as a dropped frame; threshold-gating avoids micro-stutter on weak hits and keeps feedback constants one tuning group. Target stains rejected (conflicts with crack overlays, removed shields, and moving targets). Mute-only chosen over a slider — the master bus makes a slider trivial later. Whoosh tracks normalized speed so it inherits rather than duplicates the unvalidated meter calibration (task 77).
